new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (language not in catalog, no existing statements). Type statement only (tonal, three registers, open syllables), group-level, no stress placement; consistent with Kouanga 2017 (Yakpa de Kembe: three level + two contour tones, no stress statement) already read held by the project, and with the compilers snippet reading of this same work.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level statement for the eleven Banda lects surveyed (Yakpa of Kouango = the Mid-Southern Banda point among them): open syllables and a three-register (three level tone) tonal system; the chapter says nothing about word stress/accent anywhere (whole-volume full-text index: accent 0, accentuation 0, intensité 0, tonique 0, prosodie 0, prosodique 0, trois tons 0; registres 1).
new_statements.secondary_stress: nothing (no stress statement of any kind)
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only per-lect remark for Yakpa is that its consonant and vowel system is identical to Gubu's (31 consonants, 9 ordres x 6 séries)
new_statements.identity_note: Cloarec-Heiss 1978 treats Mid-Southern Banda through 'yäkpà (de Kouango)' = Glottolog dialect Yakpa [yakp1238] of mids1243 (her other points are Linda, Langbasi, Ngbugu, Gubu, Gbi, Mbanza, Mbanja, Ngundu, Ngbundu, Kpagua); Tucker & Bryan 1956 list YAKPA (Yacoua, Yakpwa, Yakwa; Ubangi above Kouango, Kotto and Mbari rivers, Belgian Congo NE of Bosobolo), WASA (Ouassa; Bambari area), NDOKPWA/DUKPU and BONGO (Dar Kouti, Bambari) as tribes of the Banda dialect cluster (p. 33), i.e. all four Glottolog dialects of mids1243, without linguistic data.

tone_statements.citation: Kouanga, Julien. 2017. Morphologie nominale du Yākpà de Kembe. Mémoire de Master 2, Université de Bangui (SIL Language & Culture Archives). 260 pp. [Glottolog ref 680644; Yakpa = Mid-Southern Banda [bjo]]
tone_statements.quote: Le yâkpà présente trois registres de tons ponctuels : le ton haut […], le ton moyen […] et le ton bas […] ; et deux tons modulés : un ton montant (haut-bas) […] et un ton descendant (bas-haut) […]. Ce sont les voyelles qui portent les tons. Les tons jouent un rôle important au niveau des contenus lexicaux et au niveau des temps des verbes.
tone_statements.translation: Yakpa has three registers of level tones: the high tone, the mid tone and the low tone; and two contour tones: a rising tone (high-low [sic]) and a falling tone (low-high [sic]). It is the vowels that carry the tones. Tones play an important role at the level of lexical content and at the level of verb tenses.

sources.note: Ch. 1 phonology: 1.3 'Les tons' pp. 36-39 -- Yakpa is a tone language with three level tones (haut, moyen, bas) and two contour tones (montant haut-bas, descendant bas-haut) plus a moyen-bas contour in French loans; 1.4 pp. 39-40 canonical forms CV, CVCV, CVCVCV, open syllables. I 'Rappel phonologique', sec. 1.3 'Les tons' (pr. pp. 36-39): Yakpa is a tone language using tone distinctively (minimal triplets doro 'mûr/perdrix/insulter', ako, aku sets); three level tones (haut, moyen, bas) and two contour tones, which the author labels 'montant (haut-bas)' and 'descendant (bas-haut)' [labels inverted relative to usual usage, consistently so in the abbreviations list and conclusion]; vowels bear the tones; tones function lexically and in verb tense marking; 1.3.1-1.3.2…

sources.note: '2a. There appear to be three main tone levels in these languages -- High, Mid, and Low.. 2b. Stress is often responsible for changes in vowel quality and vowel length. In MAYOGO there is a tendency towards vowel length on the penultimate syllable. In NGBAKA, GBAYA, and BANDA, on the other hand, there is a tendency towards extra shortness here. Compare Eboué's BANDA spellings yaUra (dog), yabru (goat), akblo (child) with Hackett's TOGBO renderings..' -- generic BANDA (Eboué's Banda; Hackett's Togbo = togb1241), no placement rule, not tied to a Mid-Southern variety.
